ConceptChallenge.Label: The Concept Challenge
ConceptChallenge.Hint: Answer in writing: rough notes are enough. There is no right order, so begin with the group that inspires you most.

description.Label: Description
description.Prompt: What first impression do they make on a stranger, or on two people exchanging a few words?

mask.Label: The Mask
mask.Prompt: What do others believe about them at first glance, and what is only a façade?

routine.Label: The Routine
routine.Prompt: What is their typical day like? What ritual could they never give up, no matter how boring?

livelihood.Label: The Livelihood
livelihood.Prompt: What work have they done? Do they choose from passion, necessity, or jump from job to job?

spark.Label: Spark
spark.Prompt: Name three talents or virtues anyone would recognize in them.

cracks.Label: Cracks
cracks.Prompt: Name two flaws, quirks, or vices that complicate their life or relationships.

outlet.Label: Release Valve
outlet.Prompt: What makes them feel good right away: a beer, an engine, or an endless TV series?

roots.Label: Roots
roots.Prompt: What was their adolescence like? At the center of the group, on the margins, a rebel, or just passing through?

skeleton.Label: Skeleton in the Closet
skeleton.Prompt: An error, secret, or regret they pray will never resurface.

monster.Label: The Monster under the Bed
monster.Prompt: Their most irrational fear: nothing supernatural, but spiders, heights, or going home alone.

pressure.Label: Under Pressure
pressure.Prompt: When everything slips from their grasp, do they explode, shut down, run, think, lie, or analyze coldly?

redLine.Label: The Red Line
redLine.Prompt: The one thing they would refuse to do, no matter how high the stakes.

refuge.Label: The Refuge
refuge.Prompt: Where do they go, or what do they do, when they only want to disappear for a couple of hours?

superstition.Label: Profane Superstition
superstition.Prompt: An ordinary fixation or superstition, such as a recurring routine or an object chosen blindly.

beacon.Label: Beacon
beacon.Prompt: The most important human person in their life today: a partner, parent, child, friend, or trusted doctor.

thorn.Label: Thorn in the Side
thorn.Prompt: Their everyday antagonist: an intrusive neighbor, an unfair boss, a resentful ex. Why?

securityBlanket.Label: The Security Blanket
securityBlanket.Prompt: A commonplace but irreplaceable object they always carry.

lastSupper.Label: The Last Supper
lastSupper.Prompt: If the world ended tomorrow, how and with whom would they spend their final evening as a mortal?

drive.Label: Drive
drive.Prompt: The dream that makes them human, the inspiration behind their Awakening.

embodiment.Label: Embodiment
embodiment.Prompt: Up to three things they, the player, and the storyteller have in common: a hobby, fear, or ideal.

distance.Label: Distance
distance.Prompt: At least three things in which you are profoundly different: the boundary between you and them.

Scopes.Label: Scopes
Scopes.TableHint: Scopes give a Magick effect its measure, each on a scale from 0 to 7. First decide what the effect must do, then look for the Scopes needed to say it: those the effect does not touch stay at 0. Each Scope is read through two sub-scopes, alternative measures of the same thing. 0 is the base and costs nothing; each level is worth its number. The threshold is the sum of the levels of the Scopes used, and each point of threshold takes one die from the pool. An effect touching both Potency and Impact pays both. In one casting at most three Scopes rise above 0; an impossible feat takes +5 after the count.
Scopes.TableModes: In Range and Precision the Fight lens applies in combat and Narrative outside it; in Potency, Damage is for the fight and Weight for both: the Storyteller declares when a combat reading applies. In Duration the first row counts game time, the second world time. Targets, Conditions and Impact have two free lenses, good in any scene.
Scopes.TableNote: Scopes channel the generality and variability of Magick effects: think an effect in as few Scopes as possible, by need and goal.

Desc.targets: Who or what takes the effect. Effect counts targets one by one, Area takes everything inside a space.
Desc.conditions: What the effect leaves on someone and under which terms it works. The Malus is the Condition the effect puts on a target, the Complexity is the clauses that rule it.
Desc.duration: How long the effect stands. The first row counts game time, the second world time.
Desc.impact: How much the effect weighs on the story: what it changes or what it reveals. It stands apart from Potency, because an effect can be weak and weigh a lot, or strong and change nothing.
Desc.range: How far the effect reaches from the caster. To act on what you cannot see you need Correspondence, or a bond with the target (the Bridge Rule).
Desc.potency: How strong the effect is: Damage in a fight, Weight in both. How much it weighs on the story is measured by Impact.
Desc.precision: How fine the effect's choice is: in a fight the spot to hit, outside the detail to find or touch. How much what you find matters is told by Information.

impactEpic.1: Changes a detail of the scene
impactEpic.2: Shifts a moment of the scene
impactEpic.3: Decides the outcome of the scene
impactEpic.5: Changes the direction of the chapter
impactEpic.6: Bends the course of the story

targets.1: One more target, picked one by one: friends and foes sort themselves out.
targets.2: Two more targets, picked one by one.
targets.3: Three more targets, picked one by one.
targets.4: Four more targets, picked one by one.
targets.5: Five more targets, picked one by one.
targets.6: Six more targets, picked one by one.
targets.7: Seven more targets, picked one by one.

targetsArea.0: Only the point touched, no space around it.
targetsArea.1: A closed space: a room, a carriage, a lift.
targetsArea.2: A whole house or building, floors and cellars included.
targetsArea.5: A region with all its cities.
targetsArea.7: The world. Area takes everything inside, friends included: to leave them out you need a Complexity clause.

conditionsMalus.0: No Condition: the effect leaves nothing on the target.
conditionsMalus.1: Dazzled, Muffled, Shaken, Unlucky: −1 dice, or the critical that does not trigger.
conditionsMalus.2: Slowed, Disarmed, Broken, Dry. The Slowed acts last and does one thing; the others lose a family of Instruments, and the Disarmed also the equipment dice.
conditionsMalus.3: Mute, Immobilised, Stuck, Stunned: no voice, no movement, no defence or no action. Mute and Immobilised also lose Word and Body; the Stunned may mark 1 mental Health instead of losing the action.
conditionsMalus.4: Blurred, Deafened, Frightened, Knocked down: −2 dice. Knocked down applies to physical pools only, and getting up costs half a guard.
conditionsMalus.5: Blind, Deaf, Terrified: rolls based on sight or hearing are not rolled, and the Terrified does not approach the source.
conditionsMalus.6: Sick, Unfit: the Sick never exceeds 6 dice, the Unfit halves every pool.
conditionsMalus.7: Charmed, Cursed: the Charmed does not decide, the Cursed does not heal while the cause remains.

conditionsComplexity.0: The effect fires at once and applies to everything it touches. No clause.
conditionsComplexity.1: A single clause, about whom, when or where. Only for your own.
conditionsComplexity.2: Two clauses that do not touch each other. Only for your own, only at night.
conditionsComplexity.3: The effect waits for a fact to fire, or has an exception, and the Storyteller must follow the scene to know when. When the key turns; everyone but the boss.
conditionsComplexity.4: Three or four clauses together: write it down, because at the table a piece gets lost. Only for your own, only at night, while the door stays shut.
conditionsComplexity.5: Clauses that depend on one another, and one changes the meaning of another. If a stranger enters the alarm fires, but only if the door was shut.
conditionsComplexity.6: A rulebook: different cases with different answers. A friend passes, a foe stays out, a Sleeper gets lost in the corridor.
conditionsComplexity.7: A pact among several parties, with duties, exceptions and penalties for who breaks it. Who betrays the pact stays Mute until they make amends.

duration.0: The effect happens and ends within the casting turn.
duration.1: Covers an exchange of blows or a short flight.
duration.4: Stays until the end of the evening.
duration.7: Lasts as long as the chronicle.

durationWorld.7: The effect stays until someone breaks it.

impactEpic.0: Lighting a candle, spinning a coin, scenting a room.
impactEpic.1: Opening a lock, draining a phone, breaking a glass.
impactEpic.2: Distracting a guard, tripping a pursuer, cutting the power.
impactEpic.3: Bringing down a bridge, turning the crowd, blocking the exit with fire.
impactEpic.4: Making the news, emptying a building, alerting the police.
impactEpic.5: Taking a boss's lair away, breaking an alliance, closing a district.
impactEpic.6: Toppling a faction, extinguishing a Node, starting a war between Traditions.
impactEpic.7: Cracking the Veil, wiping a city off the maps, shifting the Consensus.

impactInfo.0: The time, the weather, who is in the room.
impactInfo.1: Who slept in this bed, whose pen this is, what the dog ate.
impactInfo.2: Where the guard is, which door is open, who lies at the table.
impactInfo.3: Who the traitor is, where the weapon is hidden, the password.
impactInfo.4: Where the van goes, who paid the hitman, which journalist knows too much.
impactInfo.5: Where the boss sleeps, who funds the faction, the Technocrat's real name.
impactInfo.6: Who betrayed the Tradition, why the Node went out, what a faction hides.
impactInfo.7: How the Veil was born, what came before the Consensus, where an Archmage sleeps.

range.0: You must touch the target: a hand on the shoulder, a punch.
range.1: Whoever stands next to you, without moving.
range.3: Across a courtyard or a car park.
range.4: To the end of the street.
range.5: Past the crossroads, roof to roof.
range.6: Beyond the block, where a rifle barely reaches.
range.7: As far as a marksman reaches.

rangeNarrative.1: What is before your eyes, in the scene.
rangeNarrative.2: Out of sight, in the same area: the next building, the district.
rangeNarrative.6: On the other side of the world.
rangeNarrative.7: Even without knowing where it is.

potencyDamage.0: As much damage as your Arete, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.1: Arete plus one, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.2: Arete plus two, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.3: Arete plus three, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.4: Arete plus four, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.5: Arete plus five, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.6: Arete plus six, on the target's Health.
potencyDamage.7: Arete plus seven, on the target's Health.

precision.0: You hit the target, but you do not choose where.
precision.1: A large, easy part: the torso, the bonnet.
precision.2: A large part: an arm, a leg, a car wheel.
precision.3: A small part that serves the action: the gripping hand, the steering wheel.
precision.4: An object held in hand, or a gap in the protection: the weapon, an armour joint.
precision.5: A tiny spot, often moving: an eye, the trigger.
precision.6: Something inside, unseen: an organ, the running engine.
precision.7: The point of the Pattern that makes that thing what it is.

precisionNarrative.0: The thing in general: any car, a building, a crowd.
precisionNarrative.1: One precise thing among many: that car, that person, that door.
precisionNarrative.2: A part of that thing: the engine, the pocket, the lock.
precisionNarrative.3: A small detail: the key in the lock, a screw, a button.
precisionNarrative.4: A tiny thing hidden among many: a hair on the carpet, a coin in the sand, a page in a library.
precisionNarrative.5: Something you can barely see: a speck of dust, a drop of blood, a thread.
precisionNarrative.6: What the eye cannot see: the poison in the glass, a chemical trace, a virus.
precisionNarrative.7: The smallest part of a thing: an atom, a single cell.

credo.Label: Creed
credo.Domanda: What do you believe reality is?
credo.Perche: What you believe reality is, and everything else follows: the Truth you devoted yourself to, and the voice you defend it with at the table.
credo.PercheDue: Every sect breathes its own Creeds, usually two or three: that shortlist is the beaten path to yours, not a border. The Creed assigns no points and forbids nothing: the two Spheres it suggests open up, and the Instruments it proposes come at step 7.

famiglia.Label: Family
famiglia.Domanda: The day you end up in trouble, which door will you knock on?
famiglia.Sotto: nine Traditions and ten Crafts · then the path
famiglia.Perche: But you do have a Tradition. Because it taught you to do what you know how to do, and because when you end up in trouble it is the only people who might come.
famiglia.PercheDue: Traditions survive in cabals, the group of mages you live, work and watch your back with. Do not look for the best one, because it does not exist. A Craft is a narrow road: a single Sphere and no path, and nobody will ever ask you to give up who you are to sit at the table.

bussola.Label: Compass
bussola.Domanda: Where do you want to get, what drives you now, what do you never betray?
bussola.Sotto: Ambition · Desire · one to three Convictions
bussola.Perche: Four traits written in a few lines, worth more than any score: the first two say where the character is going, the other two what keeps them human on the way.
bussola.PercheDue: The Ambition says where you want to get, and you will not get there tonight: the best ones are purely mortal. The Desire is what drives you now, and it changes as soon as you get it. The Convictions, one to three, are your moral law: absolute in form, costly in practice, double-edged. Touchstones come at step 12.

tipo.Label: Type
tipo.Domanda: Which way does your Will pass through?
tipo.Perche: With Magick the Will passes through things humans have used since they exist: the body and the voice, the object in hand, what gets consumed. With Technomagick it passes through an apparatus, and the apparatus is the point. In Hybrid the apparatus is there and does not command.
tipo.PercheDue: The Type decides the Instrument families you can use, and counts in the Arete prize: Hybrid never gets it. Machine practices (Cybernetics, Reality Hacking, Weird Science) go through Technomagick; for the others the choice is yours.

concetto.Label: Concept
concetto.Domanda: Who were you before the Awakening, in a single line?
concetto.Sotto: the Concept · the Challenge, optional, with three prizes
concetto.Perche: Who you were before the Awakening, and what you became after, in a single line. It is the filter for everything else: every dot you mark later must match this sentence.
concetto.PercheDue: It takes a real person, with an anonymous job and a tension inside, not an archetype. The Concept Challenge is twenty-one questions in three groups of seven: optional, and the game pays you back in proportion to how deep you go.

sfere.Label: Domains
sfere.Domanda: Which Creed Sphere do you open, and which power do you take in each Domain?
sfere.Sotto: three Domains · one power per Domain
sfere.Perche: The nine Spheres are the Domains of Magick. Having access to a Domain means being able to do Magick on it: there are no Sphere levels, what counts is which Domains you have and which powers you know.
sfere.PercheDue: At creation the Domains are three: the Family's, the path's and one chosen between the Creed's two. In each Domain you take a base power, or one of any Sphere if the base ones do not suit you. If you completed the whole Concept Challenge you take one more power, without prerequisites. The rest is bought with Experience, following the hierarchy of prerequisites.

strumenti.Label: Instruments
strumenti.Sotto: one Instrument per Sphere · and the Perceive one
strumenti.Perche: The things without which you do not cast. An object, a gesture, a word, a substance: something that channels your conviction. To cast you must use at least one, and it is the key in the lock.
strumenti.PercheDue: They give no dice. On the sheet they are written on two levels, the family and then your exact one: never "a knife", but my father's knife, which cuts nothing any more. The Creed and the Family propose some, and almost never the same things.

arete.Label: Arete
arete.Domanda: How much do you understand of what you do?
arete.Perche: How much your mage understands of what they are doing. At creation it is 1 for everyone, and it is the number everything else depends on: how many Spheres you can push, how high you reach.
arete.PercheDue: Now you choose nothing: mark 1, and with it Quintessence 3 and Paradox 0. Each Sphere's cap is Arete + 2. It only rises by playing, and it is the most expensive thing in the game. Advanced starts (the grade, above) start higher.

attributi.Label: Attributes
attributi.Domanda: What are you, before any training?
attributi.Perche: Nine entries in three families: what the character is before any training. The Attribute enters every roll of the game, and three of them give the base statistics.
attributi.PercheDue: Distribute a fixed shape of twenty-two dots and decide which entry gets which value. Start from the 4, which says who the character is, and finish with the 1, which is the promise of trouble: the Storyteller will use it.

abilita.Label: Skills
abilita.Sotto: nineteen dots · none above the third
abilita.Perche: Fourteen entries, a single row: what the character has learned. It adds to the Attribute to make the dice pool, and opens a Specialty at the first dot, the third and the fifth.
abilita.PercheDue: Nineteen free dots, and no entry above the third. A 3 is a trade, a 1 a smattering, a zero means you roll the Attribute alone. The fourth and fifth dot only come in play, with Experience.

vantaggi.Label: Advantages
vantaggi.Domanda: What do you have around you, what do you carry, and which troubles?
vantaggi.Sotto: seven points across Backgrounds and Merits · up to two Flaws
vantaggi.Perche: Seven points to spend in two directions: what you have outside yourself (Backgrounds) and what is yours (Merits). Three small, well-chosen traits tell more than two big ones.
vantaggi.PercheDue: Flaws are up to two points of trouble, which give back as many points to spend elsewhere: they are the only trait on the sheet that gives the Storyteller explicit permission to come after you. Take one because you want that story at the table.

ancore.Label: Touchstones
ancore.Perche: One to three ordinary people, almost always unaware Sleepers, who keep the character hooked to the world before. They give you Willpower back, and they are where they will come to get you.
ancore.PercheDue: One alone makes a tight, fierce chronicle, three make more oxygen and three times the blackmail. Choose people your mage still sees, not remembers. For each write who they are, why they matter and what they do not know: the third is where every scene comes from.

controllo.Label: Check
controllo.Perche: The whole memo: every count on the sheet against its target. When it is all green, you have a finished mage.
controllo.PercheDue: What is missing can be fixed from the sheet too: the counts on the box titles stay on with the memo, and this window reopens from the header button, at the step it was on.
